newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close easier on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close easier on profit-taking.

text.p: French shares closed slightly easier on Monday, ignoring fresh gains on Wall Street, on some profit-taking after Friday's two-and-a-half-year closing high.

On the ninth anniversary of the 1987 "Black Monday" crash, French dealers said the market's fundamentals were sound -- with easier rates and a higher dollar -- but the settlement of the October account on Thursday was spurring profit-taking.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 5.01 points or 0.23 percent at 2,180.22, while the CAC-40 futures contract fell 3.5 points at 2,186.5.
"I'm not optimistic or pessimistic this week. The markets need some time to digest the euphoria of the last few weeks," a dealer said.
* Volume was 4.6 billion francs, of which 2.9 billion on CAC-40 shares.

* Lagardere gained a further 6.26 percent to 176.60 francs on the back of winning Thomson bid. The group, which will publish first-half results tomorrow, said its Matra-BAe Dynamics joint venture won a Thai missile order whose value was estimated by industry sources at between 100 and 500 million francs.

* Metropole Television (M6) lost six percent to 420 francs as dealers feared bad news from an analysts' meeting this afternoon, mainly related to the costs of digital television. "After the disappointing (first-half) results of last week, caution pervails today," an analyst said prior to the meeting.

* Analysts raised their profit forecasts for Alcatel Alsthom, which finished down 1.35 percent at 458.80 francs on profit-taking, and Moody's Investor Service confirmed its A1 long term debt rating. Alcatel was the other bidder for Thomson.
Alcatel is in the running for a Moroccan GSM network deal.

* Schneider fell 2.23 percent to 253.90 on a Financial Times report that Britain's AMEC was expected to pay 25 million pounds for 40 percent of Schneider's Spie Batignolles, a price judged low by some investors, brokers said.
* Ingenico, rose 11.90 percent to 70.50 francs after chairman Jean-Jacques Poutrel said a proposed U.S. acquisition may increase the share value to 150 francs eventually.
* Moulinex, which closed down 1.14 percent at 95 francs, confirmed a reorganisation plan including 2,600 job cuts.

* Seita fell 3.69 percent to 196 francs on the back of the publication of a U.S. study linking cigarette-smoking and lung cancer. U.S. tobacco shares fell on Friday on expectations of lower sales and more lawsuits against cigarette makers.

* Pathe slipped 1.05 percent to 1,510 francs after The Independent newspaper said BSkyB, in which Pathe has a 17 percent stake, was planning a bid for Pearson Plc. BSkyB denied that it had such plans.
